problem_description: Compute the average temperature in K and the total energy per particle (kcal/mol) for a system of solid salt under compression. The system consists of 1000 atoms of Na^{+}, Cl^{-} arranged in a FCC crystal structure. The simulation box should cubic with dimensions from −14.2 Å to 14.2 Å (in real units) in all three directions, and periodic boundary conditions must applied in all directions. The interactions between the atoms should be described using a Lennard-Jones potential and Coulombic interactions via implemented via the lj/cut/coul/long pair style with a cutoff of 10 Å. Long-range electrostatic interactions should treated using the Particle-Particle Particle-Mesh (PPPM). Lorentz-Berthelot mixing rules (arithmetic for σ and geometric for ε) should used to define cross-interactions, along with long-range tail corrections to the LJ potential. The system must initialized by assigning velocities according to a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at 300 K. A Nosé–Hoover thermostat and barostat (fix npt) should employed to maintain the system at a constant temperature of 300 K and anisotropic pressure of 1 atm, with damping parameters of 100 fs (thermostat) and 1000 fs (barostat). After an initial equilibration run of 5000 steps, the system underwent a controlled compression process. This was achieved by iteratively scaling the simulation box along the x-direction by a factor of 0.99 over 20 cycles. Each compression step was followed by a short equilibration run of 500 steps, allowing the system to relax between successive deformations.
